(طَوَطَ) الطَّاءُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالطَّاءُ كَلِمَتَانِ إِنْ صَحَّتَا. يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ الطَّوْطَ الْقُطْنُ. وَالطَّوْطُ: الرَّجُلُ الطَّوِيلُ.
[بَابُ الطَّاءِ وَالْيَاءِ وَمَا يَثْلُثُهُمَا]

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Characteristic adjective of مَطَّ (maṭṭa, “to stretch”), from the root م ط ط (m ṭ ṭ); nominalized in the meaning "rubber".

Unknown, possibly an ancient loan from Hebrew טִיט (ṭīṭ, “mud; clay”) or Moabite or Edomite identical to the Arabic طِين (ṭīn), the suffixation of ـَان (-ān) in general more likely Northwest Semitic, in view of the plant’s tunic dark brown, coarsely reticulate-fibrous bulb resembling a globe of clay.
